clue.text: Bird, dogs and parasite found in wood in Manhattan?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, such as a rooster
to dog someone is to follow them, which is what tails means as a verb
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A list of creatures, a bird, dogs and a bug, turning up in a New York woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Manhattan looks like the New York borough, but here it is the whisky cocktail, and the wood in it is the little stick holding the cherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a mixed drink, and the slim wooden spike skewering its garnish is a cocktail-party item, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sportingly get around with nothing on entire bust? I'm not sure

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of entire are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: er is the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: Someone doubtfully wondering whether a whole statue could be got round with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpted torso, which suits 'nothing on', but it signals breaking up: RIENTE comes from the letters of 'entire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orienteering is a sport of finding your way round a course with map and compass, so to do it is to navigate in sporting fashion.

clue.text: What's taken up by chef in kitchen

definitions.text: What's taken up by chef in kitchen

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a cook picks up while working at the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'What's' alone as the definition, but the whole clue defines the answer: the hidden EFINK, read upwards in this down clue, is also what a chef takes up. So it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook's essential tool is a blade, the thing a chef lifts and uses all day in a kitchen.

clue.text: Tired no one out

definitions.meaning: everybody is inside, with nobody left out

explanation.surface: A weary person, with nobody excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for exhausted, and read literally it says every person is in.

clue.text: Where you take off home after a filling repast

indicators.note: after says the home word comes behind the meal
filling says the a goes inside the meal word

parts.note: a repast is a meal, here lunch
pad is slang for a home or flat

explanation.surface: Leaving the house after eating a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like departing the house, but it is a rocket's lift-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the platform from which rockets lift off.

clue.text: Passes through river cooler than the others

indicators.note: through says the passes word sits inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
to pass, in the sense of pass away, is to die

explanation.surface: Something passing across a river that is chillier than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' suggests temperature; it means more fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable or cool, and the superlative form means the most fashionable of the group.

clue.text: Worry, dropping a maiden's cosmetic

indicators.note: dropping says the a falls lower in this down entry, moving later in the worry word

parts.note: to worry is to care, be concerned
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Ceasing to fret over a young woman's make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a' looks like losing the A, but it only moves down: CARE becomes CREA, then M is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Face cream is a common skincare product, a cosmetic applied to the skin.

clue.text: Bear with lodging that is hot and hope for change

parts.note: an inn is a place offering lodging
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: for change says the letters of hot and hope are switched around

explanation.surface: Putting up with cheap lodgings that are too warm, and hoping things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb, tolerate, but it is the animal: A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy. 'for change' shuffles HOT and HOPE into THEPOOH.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of A. A. Milne's children's stories is a teddy, a famous fictional ursine.

clue.text: Retiring seems doubtful for old German performer

indicators.note: doubtful says the letters are uncertain in order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Whether a German performer of the past should step down seems uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meistersingers were members of German guilds of poets and musicians in the 14th to 16th centuries, so an old German singer.

clue.text: Early version of Latin 11

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figures 1 and 1 read as two Roman ones, I I

explanation.surface: An early draft of a Latin text cross-referenced to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to the clue for 11 across, but it is just two ones, II, mixed in with LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means at the beginning, first in time, which is a synonym of early.

clue.text: Here fashion mag contains tab for stringed instrument

parts.note: for a British newspaper, here is the UK

indicators.note: contains says the tab letter goes inside the magazine name

parts.note: Elle is a well-known fashion magazine
a tab is a tablet, specifically ecstasy, E

explanation.surface: A local fashion magazine carrying a guitar tablature for a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tab' looks like guitar tablature, which suits the instrument, but it is a pill of ecstasy, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ukulele (spelt this way as a variant) is a small four-stringed guitar-like instrument from Hawaii.

clue.text: Unaffiliated to Welby for the present?

parts.note: non- means not belonging to
Justin Welby was Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England, CE

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a person unconnected with the archbishop is acting temporarily.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone not of the Church of England is NON-CE. 'For the nonce' is an old phrase meaning for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives in the idiom for the nonce, meaning for the present occasion or time being.

clue.text: Pharisee's overcome problem in penning laws

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the laws word goes inside
overcome, read as turned over, says the words problem and in are reversed

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a code is a body of laws

explanation.surface: A Pharisee has overcome a difficulty involving the drafting of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' turns SUM IN into NIMUS, which then pens CODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee in John's Gospel who visits Jesus by night.

clue.text: Polish pieces accepted by top journalist

indicators.note: accepted by says the pieces go inside the journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A senior journalist accepting bits of copy and smoothing them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' could be the nationality; it is the verb, refine.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish a text is to improve it by correcting and refining, which is a synonym of revise or amend.

clue.text: Move from A to B and awkwardly drag blue English cases

parts.note: blue means sad, down

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of drag are put together clumsily, in a new order

explanation.surface: Clumsily hauling some sad English boxes from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move from A to B' suggests travel; it is a fall from grade A to grade B. 'awkwardly' turns DRAG into GRAD; 'cases' is taken here as joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower in rank or rating is the sense, as when a mark or classification slips one letter.

clue.text: Puff maintaining acceleration, then running round to put in a dash

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the other letters sit inside the puff word

parts.note: puff is exaggerated promotion, hype

indicators.note: running round says the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

explanation.surface: A sprinter puffing, keeping up speed and running round to make a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: The sprinting imagery makes 'dash' a run, but it is the punctuation mark. 'running round' gives HENAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To join words with the short punctuation line called a hyphen is to insert a dash between them.

clue.text: Latvian present's wrapped, a decoction

indicators.note: wrapped says the present word goes round the Latvian

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
a Latvian is a Balt, from the Baltic states

explanation.surface: A gift from Latvia has been giftwrapped, with a boiled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, matching 'wrapped', but means HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoction is a drink made by boiling plants, as in a brewed infusion of herbs.

clue.text: Bedazzled throng following One Direction

indicators.note: following says the throng comes after the other parts

parts.note: one is the article a
west is a compass direction
a ruck is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A crowd of starstruck fans following the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a British boy band, but here 'One' is A and 'Direction' is WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dazzled and overwhelmed is the meaning; to be filled with wonder is a synonym of bedazzled.

clue.text: Warder hid criminal unable to be changed

indicators.note: criminal here is a judgement on how the letters are treated, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prison officer hid a crook who could not be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuitry built into the hardware is fixed and permanent, hence inflexible or unchangeable.

clue.text: Sarkozy's very small — it's a bit of a shock

parts.note: Nicolas Sarkozy, a French president, would say tres for very

explanation.surface: Remarking that a short French politician gives people a slight start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mass of it, and a curl or lock is a piece of that.

clue.text: Where china's buried for German nobleman

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a mate's is a pal's
where someone is buried is the grave

explanation.surface: Wondering where porcelain lies interred, for an aristocrat from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where china's buried' reads as a pal's grave. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a high-ranking German noble title.

clue.text: Story's engrossing for one lord

indicators.note: engrossing means absorbing, so the story word takes in the other piece

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
for one means for example, e.g.

explanation.surface: A tale that captivates an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms the word means a superior to whom allegiance is owed, a sovereign or lord.

clue.text: The king's mischievous horse bolts

indicators.note: bolts means runs off, so the horse letter leaves

parts.note: elvish means like an elf, impish and mischievous
horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: A monarch's naughty steed runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like the steed that bolts, but is drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was dubbed the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: It's to put in information board

indicators.note: put in says the word to goes inside the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An instruction to add something to a noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'information board' reads as a noticeboard, but 'board' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a bus or train is to climb aboard it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: It's left and right and it's all over for him

parts.note: left means departed, gone

explanation.surface: A man whose position has been abandoned on every side, with his end at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person doomed or past saving is a lost cause, someone finished.

clue.text: Public scoffs a starter of cheese and ham

indicators.note: scoffs means eats greedily, so the public word swallows the other letters

parts.note: overt means open, public

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so the first letter of cheese

explanation.surface: Someone in public wolfing down cheese and ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat; it is the verb for performing too theatrically.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a showy, exaggerated performer, and as a verb it means to perform too theatrically.

clue.text: Opening game turned around by header from Eden Hazard

parts.note: a vent is an opening

indicators.note: turned around says the game letters are read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: a header is at the top, so the first letter of Eden

explanation.surface: A football match turned around by a headed goal from Belgian star Eden Hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden Hazard was a Chelsea footballer; the name is split, 'Hazard' being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to risk it, as in hazarding a guess, a synonym of to dare or chance.

clue.text: Soldiers needing vehicle when everyone's out

parts.note: generals are high-ranking soldiers
a trike is a tricycle, a vehicle

explanation.surface: Troops needing transport at a time when everyone is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means on strike, not absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage in which workers across all industries walk out together is a nationwide stoppage of labour.
